report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content.

Reasoning:
- The highest-norm cells (especially layers 18–25 across positions 1–4) decode via the logit lens to a very tight cluster of food/culinary terms: “cooking,” “Cooking,” “baking,” “Restaurant,” “restaurant,” “Chef,” “kitchen,” “Kitchen,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “microwave,” “oven,” “Professional/professional,” “Chef,” “culinary,” “Cooking Professional,” etc. This pattern is consistent across many layers and positions, not a one-off.
- Mid layers also surface related formal/industry words (“culinary,” “Restaurant,” “professional,” “technical,” “Innovation”) alongside some more general academic/professional terms (“dissertation,” “sciences”), but the dominant, repeated theme is culinary/food preparation and restaurant vocabulary.
- The difference magnitude concentrates in later layers, suggesting a shift in output vocabulary/style rather than low-level tokenization effects.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B appears domain-shifted toward food/culinary/recipe/restaurant text (and associated “professional” framing).
